claims.title: Adulis named in the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea
claims.summary: The Greek navigational handbook describes Adulis as the principal, legally regulated port serving the Aksumite hinterland, trading ivory, rhinoceros horn, tortoise shell and other goods.

sources.label: The Ancient Red Sea Port of Adulis, Eritrea (Eritro-British Expedition report)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-50-adulis-named-in-the-periplus-of-the-erythraean, claim TL:ERI:event:50:adulis-named-in-the-periplus-of-the-erythraean, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Aksum emerges as a Red Sea trading empire
claims.summary: Aksum consolidates control of the northern highlands and the port of Adulis, growing into a major commercial power linking Rome, Arabia and India.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-100-aksum-emerges-as-a-red-sea-trading-empire, claim TL:ERI:event:100:aksum-emerges-as-a-red-sea-trading-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Aksumite coinage
claims.summary: Aksumite kings begin minting gold, silver and bronze coins, advertising the kingdom's wealth and its place among the great powers of the age.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-270-aksumite-coinage, claim TL:ERI:event:270:aksumite-coinage, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Decline of Aksum and Adulis
claims.summary: Shifting trade routes and the rise of Islam on the Arabian shore erode Red Sea commerce; Adulis fades and Aksum's power contracts inland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-700-decline-of-aksum-and-adulis, claim TL:ERI:event:700:decline-of-aksum-and-adulis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Beja ascendancy on the coast
claims.summary: After the fall of Aksum, Beja confederacies dominate the caravan routes and coastal trade of what is now Eritrea, holding sway in the Massawa region for centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-740-beja-ascendancy-on-the-coast, claim TL:ERI:event:740:beja-ascendancy-on-the-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Sultanate of Dahlak
claims.summary: The Dahlak Islands become a wealthy Muslim sultanate controlling pearl fisheries and the trade between the Red Sea and the Christian highlands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1000-rise-of-the-sultanate-of-dahlak, claim TL:ERI:event:1000:rise-of-the-sultanate-of-dahlak, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Massawa grows as a leading port
claims.summary: Massawa develops into the principal harbour of the coast, mediating trade between the highland interior and the Arabian Peninsula.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1300-massawa-grows-as-a-leading-port, claim TL:ERI:event:1300:massawa-grows-as-a-leading-port, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottomans capture Massawa
claims.summary: Ottoman forces under Ozdemir Pasha take Massawa from the highland kingdom, bringing the Eritrean coast under the Ottoman Empire and ending local dynastic control.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1557-ottomans-capture-massawa, claim TL:ERI:event:1557:ottomans-capture-massawa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman Habesh province established
claims.summary: After taking Massawa, the Ottomans organise their Red Sea holdings as the province of Habesh, ruling the coast through local agents.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1557-ottoman-habesh-province-established, claim TL:ERI:event:1557:ottoman-habesh-province-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Egyptian administration of Massawa
claims.summary: Egypt, with Ottoman consent, takes over the administration of Massawa and the coast, extending its influence toward the highlands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1865-egyptian-administration-of-massawa, claim TL:ERI:event:1865:egyptian-administration-of-massawa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Italy gains a foothold at Assab
claims.summary: An Italian shipping company acquires the bay of Assab on the southern Red Sea coast, Italy's first toehold on the future Eritrean shore.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1869-italy-gains-a-foothold-at-assab, claim TL:ERI:event:1869:italy-gains-a-foothold-at-assab, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Italy occupies Massawa
claims.summary: As Egypt withdraws amid the Mahdist crisis, Italian troops occupy Massawa, the key port of the coast, beginning Italy's drive to build a colony.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1885-italy-occupies-massawa, claim TL:ERI:event:1885:italy-occupies-massawa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Colony of Eritrea proclaimed
claims.summary: Italy unites its Red Sea holdings into the colony of Eritrea, promoted as its colonia primogenita or 'first-born colony', with the capital initially at Massawa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1890-colony-of-eritrea-proclaimed, claim TL:ERI:event:1890:colony-of-eritrea-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Adwa
claims.summary: Advancing from Eritrea, an Italian army is destroyed by Emperor Menelik II at Adwa, the worst defeat of a European army in Africa, securing Ethiopian sovereignty and fixing Eritrea's southern frontier.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1896-battle-of-adwa, claim TL:ERI:event:1896:battle-of-adwa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Asmara becomes the colonial capital
claims.summary: The colonial seat is moved from Massawa to the highland town of Asmara, later rebuilt as a planned modernist city.

sources.label: Asmara: A Modernist City of Africa

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1897-asmara-becomes-the-colonial-capital, claim TL:ERI:event:1897:asmara-becomes-the-colonial-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conquest of Ethiopia launched from Eritrea
claims.summary: Italian forces invade Ethiopia from Eritrea, taking Addis Ababa in May 1936; Eritrea is absorbed into Italian East Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1935-conquest-of-ethiopia-launched-from-eritrea, claim TL:ERI:event:1935:conquest-of-ethiopia-launched-from-eritrea, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British defeat Italy at Keren
claims.summary: Allied forces overcome Italian troops at the Battle of Keren; Asmara and Massawa surrender, ending Italian rule and beginning British military administration.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1941-british-defeat-italy-at-keren, claim TL:ERI:event:1941:british-defeat-italy-at-keren, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British military administration begins
claims.summary: Following the Allied victory at Keren, Britain administers Eritrea for the next decade while its post-war status is debated.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1941-british-military-administration-begins, claim TL:ERI:event:1941:british-military-administration-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: UN federation with Ethiopia
claims.summary: Under UN Resolution 390 A (V) of 1950, Eritrea becomes an autonomous unit federated with Ethiopia, keeping its own parliament, flag and control of internal affairs.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Eritrea
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1952-un-federation-with-ethiopia, claim TL:ERI:event:1952:un-federation-with-ethiopia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Armed struggle begins at Mount Adal
claims.summary: Hamid Idris Awate and a small ELF band fire on Ethiopian forces, the conventional start of the thirty-year Eritrean War of Independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1961-armed-struggle-begins-at-mount-adal, claim TL:ERI:event:1961:armed-struggle-begins-at-mount-adal, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Haile Selassie annexes Eritrea
claims.summary: After steadily eroding Eritrean autonomy, the emperor dissolves the federation and annexes Eritrea as a province, hardening the independence war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1962-haile-selassie-annexes-eritrea, claim TL:ERI:event:1962:haile-selassie-annexes-eritrea, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the EPLF
claims.summary: The Eritrean People's Liberation Front splits from the ELF and becomes the dominant, Marxist-led nationalist movement waging the war.

sources.label: Eritrea: The Independence Struggle and the Struggles of Independence
sources.publisher: Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1970-rise-of-the-eplf, claim TL:ERI:event:1970:rise-of-the-eplf, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: EPLF captures Asmara
claims.summary: As the Derg regime collapses in Ethiopia, EPLF forces enter Asmara, winning de facto independence and forming a provisional government.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1991-eplf-captures-asmara, claim TL:ERI:event:1991:eplf-captures-asmara, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence referendum
claims.summary: Eritreans vote overwhelmingly for independence in a UN-monitored referendum, with near-unanimous approval on a high turnout.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Eritrea
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1993-independence-referendum, claim TL:ERI:event:1993:independence-referendum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Formal independence
claims.summary: Eritrea proclaims itself a sovereign state and is admitted to the United Nations days later; Isaias Afwerki becomes its first president.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Eritrea
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1993-formal-independence, claim TL:ERI:event:1993:formal-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Border war with Ethiopia
claims.summary: A dispute over Badme escalates into a full-scale war that kills tens of thousands and displaces more than a million before a ceasefire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-1998-border-war-with-ethiopia, claim TL:ERI:event:1998:border-war-with-ethiopia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Algiers Agreement
claims.summary: Eritrea and Ethiopia sign the Algiers peace agreement; a boundary commission later awards Badme to Eritrea, but Ethiopia refuses to withdraw, leaving a frozen stand-off.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-2000-algiers-agreement, claim TL:ERI:event:2000:algiers-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Entrenched one-party rule
claims.summary: Promised elections and the ratified constitution are shelved; indefinite national service and bans on independent press, parties and religion make Eritrea one of the world's most closed states.

sources.label: Eritrea-Ethiopia Peace Deal Offers Hope for Reform

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-2001-entrenched-one-party-rule, claim TL:ERI:event:2001:entrenched-one-party-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Peace with Ethiopia
claims.summary: Isaias Afwerki and Abiy Ahmed sign a declaration formally ending the border war, though internal repression in Eritrea continues largely unchanged.

sources.label: Eritrea-Ethiopia Peace Deal Offers Hope for Reform

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Eritrea: From the Red Sea ports of Aksum to Africa's longest war of independence and one of its most closed states.", terralore.co/country/ERI/chronicle#ev-2018-peace-with-ethiopia, claim TL:ERI:event:2018:peace-with-ethiopia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
